findings.status: independent corroboration and hull-specific source refinement of REVIEW-PLAN-POLYGON-MIXED-SCALE-AREA-001; do not count the same first failure twice
findings.first_contract: ArchitecturalPlanPoint accepts all finite f32 coordinates. PlanPolygon promises finite, nondegenerate counterclockwise convex vertices and calculates its area using f64 differences after widening. PlanHull uses the same f64 difference-and-cross operation to distinguish segment and area.
findings.symbolic_source_reasoning: Let t=2^-100, exactly representable as a positive finite f32, and take A=(t,0), B=(2,2), C=(1,1). The exact real determinant (B−A)×(C−A) is t > 0, so A,B,C form a nondegenerate counterclockwise triangle. In binary64 subtraction, 2−t rounds to 2 and 1−t rounds to 1; the calculated translated vectors become (2,2) and (1,1), whose computed cross and signed area are zero. Source control flow therefore returns DegeneratePolygon before later checks. In the monotone-hull sorting order A,C,B, both forward and reverse crosses round to zero, so its source algorithm discards C and classifies the set as a Segment. This is symbolic IEEE-754 arithmetic, not a product invocation, generated fixture, probe or test.
findings.consumers: CollisionCuboid::ground_contact projects checked 3D corners/intersections to ArchitecturalPlanPoint and classifies via PlanHull. BuildingCollision::ground_floor_footprint returns Some only for an Area; compiled city seating and envelope paths map None to MissingBearing. These references establish possible downstream roles, not that any supported cuboid, building, or real plan can produce the symbolic point set.

lenses.assessment: Plan-point admission retains a finite owner before hull calculations and selected consumers; WallLocalFrame retains raw origin/basis. Existing owner q407 and polygon precision finding remain distinct.
RoomIndex and StoreyIndex are purpose-specific despite sharing OrdinalError; ArchitecturalPlanPoint already owns finite plan coordinates and must not be conflated with scene or spatial vectors.
Point constructors and Serde reject nonfinite pairs; ordered polygon checks size, area, direction and duplicates, yet a valid mixed-scale triangle can be falsely rejected by f64 cancellation.
Widening f32 inputs to f64 avoids range overflow but loses small offsets at wide exponent gaps; local orientation and area signs need the supported numeric contract.
Finite vertices do not alone establish a polygon; encoded ordinal does not establish membership; wall origin, tangent, outward and room links require correlated source context.
Architectural point, scene point, room/storey ordinal, wire representation and native coordinate arithmetic have distinct owners. Maintain error provenance through the actual external boundary.
OrdinalError is intentionally shared error provenance rather than duplicate index authority; PlanHull and polygon admission share cross arithmetic but are not automatically the same recipient.

Each selected file is byte-identical across P16 object and compared revisions, not evidence the snapshot or runtime behaviors match. Preserve intentional round-before-below-ground and exact zero/point/segment semantics.
GroundContact and PlanHull explicitly distinguish dimensional cases; RecipeOrdinalRole carries a semantic tag to the shared error. No semantic boolean replacement established.

Manual StoreyIndex Serialize performs checked narrowing and contextual error conversion; automatic transparent derive could change capacity behavior. ArchitecturalPlanPoint manual Deserialize re-admits finite components.
Finite point, counterclockwise convex polygon, actual ground-contact dimensionality and building-relative identity are different contracts; validity of one does not prove another.
PlanGeometryError and ordinal errors use typed variants/source causes; display text is a presentation boundary, not evidence of an internal string protocol.
u16 packing capacity, rounded elevation station and exact-zero geometric predicates have distinct semantics; avoiding overflow does not establish exact orientation.
